evidence: Receiving DO2 drops stepwise from 12.82 mg/L at 46.0 h to 5.85 mg/L at 46.2 h and then steadily to 3.27 mg/L at 52.0 h
Receiving P assay: 1.14 g/L (36 h), 2.92 g/L (48 h) — production active during the DO decline
All three source batches at the same 48 h mark have DO2 of 10.8–11.5 mg/L, showing receiving-process oxygen stress is anomalous
Constraint: minimum DO 2.0 mg/L; action bounds: combined = feed x0.8, air x1.15
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation shows an abrupt oxygen-supply/use imbalance: DO2 fell from ~12.8 mg/L at 46.0 h to 5.85 mg/L at 46.2 h and continued declining to 3.27 mg/L at the 52 h decision point, with P = 2.92 g/L at 48 h (product still accumulating). No source batch ever dropped below ~7.4 mg/L, so this is a receiving-process anomaly (e.g., elevated oxygen uptake outstripping transfer). DO2 is trending toward the 2.0 mg/L floor within a few hours on the current KEEP trajectory. A bounded combined intervention (feed x0.8 to cut oxygen demand and air x1.15 to raise transfer) addresses both sides of the imbalance while retaining product mass; feed reduction alone (x0.8, x0.6) slows production and strong reduction (x0.6) risks yield loss; air increase alone (x1.15 cap) is likely insufficient given the steep ~0.5 mg/L/h decline and has less margin against the constraint. Stop would zero counted production and is unwarranted since the culture is still productive and above the DO floor.
args.uncertainty: Uncertain whether the DO decline is driven by a step change in uptake (suggesting feed control) or a drop in transfer efficiency (suggesting air); combined covers both at moderate magnitude. Unknown hidden receiving parameters mean the x1.15 air ceiling may not fully restore DO, and x0.8 feed cuts may sacrifice some titer; hidden state could also recover spontaneously (KEEP), but the monotone decline near the 2.0 mg/L floor makes inaction riskier. Timing/actuation lags are unmodeled, so the trajectory could dip below 2.0 mg/L before effects materialize.
